title: Mechanical Vibrations
description: This syllabus treats vibrations as the bridge among dynamics, system modeling, measurement, and design. Students move from 1-DOF response to modal analysis, continuous systems, random vibration, experimental testing, and engineering control applications.

topics.title: Vibration Modeling, Linearization, and Equation Formulation
topics.description: Model mechanical systems as lumped-parameter oscillators using force, energy, and equivalent-parameter ideas.

children.title: Mechanical Oscillator Idealizations
children.description: Students learn how real machines and structures become solvable vibration models.

children.title: Mass, stiffness, damping, inertia, compliance, and constraint
Lumped-parameter model, distributed-parameter model, rigid body, and flexible body
Translational vibration, torsional vibration, bending vibration, and axial vibration
Degree of freedom, generalized coordinate, equilibrium position, and small motion
Equation-of-Motion Methods
children.description: This subtopic gives students several reliable ways to derive vibration equations.

children.title: Free-body diagram, Newton's second law, moment equation, and D'Alembert principle
Energy method, kinetic energy, potential energy, and generalized force
Lagrange equation, virtual work, and generalized coordinate
Equivalent stiffness, equivalent mass, and equivalent damping
Linearization and Model Assumptions
children.description: The point is to know what the model keeps, what it drops, and when that is acceptable.

children.title: Static equilibrium, perturbation coordinate, small-angle approximation, and Taylor linearization
Linear spring, viscous damper, Coulomb friction, and structural damping idealizations
Initial condition, boundary condition, forcing function, and parameter uncertainty
Model validation, natural frequency check, and dimensional consistency

topics.title: Free Vibration of Undamped Single-Degree-of-Freedom Systems
topics.description: Analyze natural frequency and free response of ideal 1-DOF spring-mass and torsional systems.

children.title: Natural Frequency and Simple Harmonic Motion
children.description: Students learn the baseline oscillation behavior before damping or forcing complicates it.

children.title: Spring-mass system, torsional oscillator, pendulum approximation, and equivalent oscillator
Natural circular frequency, natural frequency in Hz, period, and phase angle
Amplitude, displacement, velocity, acceleration, and initial conditions
Energy exchange between kinetic and potential energy
Analytical Solution and Response Interpretation
children.description: This subtopic connects the differential equation to physical motion.

children.title: Second-order homogeneous differential equation
Characteristic equation, sine/cosine form, and amplitude-phase form
Initial displacement, initial velocity, and response envelope
Phase plane, state variables, and response plots
Equivalent Systems and Design Sensitivity
children.description: The goal is to see how mass and stiffness changes alter vibration behavior.

children.title: Equivalent spring in series, equivalent spring in parallel, and torsional stiffness
Effective mass, mass moment of inertia, and radius of gyration
Frequency tuning, stiffness change, mass change, and sensitivity
Static deflection method and frequency estimation

topics.title: Damped Single-Degree-of-Freedom Vibration
topics.description: Study viscous, Coulomb, and structural damping and how damping changes transient response.

children.title: Viscous Damping Model
children.description: Students learn the most common mathematical damping model and its response classes.

children.title: Damping coefficient, critical damping coefficient, damping ratio, and damped natural frequency
Underdamped response, critically damped response, and overdamped response
Logarithmic decrement, decay envelope, and settling time
Quality factor, bandwidth connection, and energy dissipation
Other Damping Mechanisms
children.description: Real structures dissipate energy in more than one way, so students need the model vocabulary.

children.title: Coulomb friction, dry friction, structural damping, hysteretic damping, and material damping
Equivalent viscous damping and energy-equivalent damping
Air damping, fluid damping, joint damping, and frictional interfaces
Damping identification from free decay
Transient Response and Design Implications
children.description: The point is to connect damping to shock response, settling, and vibration control.

children.title: Overshoot, peak time, time constant, and decay rate
Impulse-like initial condition and ringdown
Damping trade-offs in instruments, vehicles, machines, and structures
Underdamped oscillation avoidance and rapid settling design

topics.title: Forced Harmonic Vibration, Resonance, and Frequency Response
topics.description: Analyze steady-state response to sinusoidal forcing and interpret resonance, phase, and transmissibility.

children.title: Steady-State Harmonic Response
children.description: Students learn how systems respond to sinusoidal forces at different frequencies.

children.title: Harmonic force, excitation frequency, frequency ratio, and steady-state amplitude
Dynamic magnification factor, phase angle, and complex response
Particular solution, transient solution, and total response
Force excitation, displacement response, velocity response, and acceleration response
Resonance and Frequency Response Functions
children.description: This subtopic makes resonance quantitative and visible.

children.title: Resonance frequency, peak response, half-power bandwidth, and damping effect
Frequency response function, receptance, mobility, and accelerance
Bode magnitude plot, Bode phase plot, and Nyquist plot
Anti-resonance, phase crossover, and response peak interpretation
Rotating and Reciprocating Excitation Preview
children.description: The goal is to connect harmonic response to common machine vibration sources.

children.title: Rotating unbalance, eccentric mass, centrifugal force, and whirl speed
Reciprocating engine forces and harmonic components
Synchronous excitation, forcing order, and order tracking preview
Resonance avoidance and speed-range restrictions

topics.title: General Forcing, Impulse Response, and Time-Domain Methods
topics.description: Extend vibration response to impulse, step, arbitrary, and periodic forcing.

children.title: Impulse, Step, and Arbitrary Forcing
children.description: Students learn how vibration systems respond when forcing is not a single sine wave.

children.title: Unit impulse, impulse response, step response, ramp input, and pulse excitation
Duhamel integral, convolution, and superposition
Shock response, transient load, and impact force
Initial conditions plus external forcing
Periodic and Fourier-Based Forcing
children.description: This subtopic connects repeated non-sinusoidal loads to harmonic components.

children.title: Fourier series, harmonic component, fundamental frequency, and spectrum
Square wave, sawtooth, pulse train, and rotating machinery harmonics
Response to each harmonic and modal superposition of harmonic responses
Beat phenomenon and close-frequency forcing
Numerical Time Integration
children.description: The point is to solve vibration problems that do not have convenient closed forms.

children.title: State-space form, first-order system, and numerical integration
Euler method, Runge-Kutta method, central difference method, and Newmark-beta method
Time step, stability, accuracy, and numerical damping
MATLAB/Python simulation and validation against analytical cases

topics.title: Base Excitation, Rotating Unbalance, and Vibration Isolation
topics.description: Analyze vibrations caused by moving supports, rotating machinery, and transmitted forces.

children.title: Base Excitation
children.description: Students learn how moving supports drive vibration even without a direct applied force.

children.title: Base displacement, relative displacement, absolute displacement, and support motion
Road input, floor vibration, seismic motion, and shaker table input
Displacement transmissibility and acceleration transmissibility
Low-frequency following and high-frequency isolation
Vibration Isolation
children.description: This subtopic shows how mounts and isolators reduce transmitted motion or force.

children.title: Force transmissibility, isolation frequency, static deflection, and mount stiffness
Isolation region, amplification region, and transmissibility ratio
Elastomer mount, spring isolator, dashpot, and tuned support
Machine foundation, sensitive instrument isolation, and vehicle suspension
Rotating Unbalance and Machine Vibration
children.description: The goal is to diagnose one of the most common machinery vibration problems.

children.title: Unbalance force, eccentricity, rotor speed, and synchronous response
Critical speed, rotor whirl, and balancing plane
Single-plane balancing and two-plane balancing as practical ideas
Fan, pump, motor, turbine, and shaft examples

topics.title: Two-Degree-of-Freedom Systems and Coupled Oscillations
topics.description: Study coupled coordinates, normal modes, mode shapes, and beating in 2-DOF systems.

children.title: Coupled Equations and Normal Modes
children.description: Students learn how multiple coordinates interact through mass and stiffness coupling.

children.title: Two masses, coupled springs, generalized coordinates, and coupled equations
Mass matrix, stiffness matrix, and determinant condition
Natural frequencies, mode shapes, and modal vectors
In-phase mode, out-of-phase mode, and physical interpretation
Modal Coordinates and Beating
children.description: This subtopic shows how coupled motion can be understood as a sum of simpler motions.

children.title: Coordinate transformation, normal coordinate, modal coordinate, and decoupling
Orthogonality in a simple 2-DOF setting
Beat frequency, energy exchange, and close natural frequencies
Initial condition projection onto modes
Dynamic Vibration Absorbers
children.description: The point is to use a second degree of freedom to control vibration deliberately.

children.title: Tuned mass damper, absorber mass, absorber stiffness, and tuning frequency
Primary system, absorber system, and anti-resonance
Den Hartog tuning idea and damping in absorbers
Building damper, machinery absorber, and vehicle application examples

topics.title: Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Systems and Matrix Methods
topics.description: Generalize vibration analysis to finite systems using mass, damping, and stiffness matrices.

children.title: Matrix Formulation
children.description: Students learn to express finite vibration systems compactly and computationally.

children.title: Mass matrix, damping matrix, stiffness matrix, force vector, and displacement vector
Lumped mass, consistent mass, influence coefficient, and stiffness assembly
Symmetric matrix, positive definiteness, and boundary constraint
Finite element vibration model preview
Eigenvalue Problem
children.description: This subtopic is the mathematical core of MDOF free vibration.

children.title: Generalized eigenvalue problem, characteristic equation, eigenvalue, and eigenvector
Natural frequency, mode shape, repeated root, and rigid-body mode
Mass-normalized mode, stiffness-normalized mode, and modal matrix
Numerical eigensolver and interpretation of computed modes
Forced Response of MDOF Systems
children.description: The point is to predict response when many coordinates move together.

children.title: Harmonic force vector, frequency response matrix, and dynamic stiffness matrix
Damping matrix, proportional damping, Rayleigh damping, and non-proportional damping
Direct integration, modal superposition, and steady-state response
Participation of modes and truncation error

topics.title: Modal Analysis, Orthogonality, and Modal Superposition
topics.description: Use modal coordinates and orthogonality to decouple linear vibration systems.

children.title: Orthogonality and Normalization
children.description: Students learn why modes can decouple linear systems.

children.title: Mass orthogonality, stiffness orthogonality, and modal normalization
Modal mass, modal stiffness, modal damping, and modal force
Mode shape scaling and sign convention
Complete modal basis and modal truncation
Modal Superposition
children.description: This subtopic turns complex MDOF response into sums of modal responses.

children.title: Modal coordinate, modal participation factor, and generalized force
Impulse response, harmonic response, and transient response by modes
Dominant mode, residual flexibility, and missing mass
Initial condition expansion and forced response expansion
Experimental and Operational Modal Analysis Preview
children.description: The goal is to connect theoretical modes to measured structures.

children.title: Experimental modal analysis, operational modal analysis, and operating deflection shape
FRF curve fitting, mode identification, and modal assurance criterion
Impact hammer test, shaker test, and sensor placement
Correlation between test and finite element model

topics.title: Continuous Systems and Approximate Methods
topics.description: Analyze strings, rods, shafts, beams, and plates as distributed-parameter vibration systems.

children.title: Distributed-Parameter Vibration Models
children.description: Students learn that many real structures have infinitely many modes.

children.title: String vibration, longitudinal rod vibration, torsional shaft vibration, and beam vibration
Partial differential equation, boundary condition, and initial condition
Wave speed, natural frequency sequence, and mode function
Node, antinode, standing wave, and orthogonal functions
Beam and Shaft Vibration
children.description: This subtopic covers the most common mechanical/structural continuous systems.

children.title: Euler-Bernoulli beam, bending stiffness EI, mass per length, and boundary conditions
Simply supported, clamped, free, and cantilever boundary conditions
Torsional vibration of shafts and polar inertia
Critical speed of shafts and rotating machinery connection
Approximate Methods
children.description: The point is to estimate natural frequencies and modes when exact solutions are hard.

children.title: Rayleigh quotient, assumed modes, Galerkin method, and Ritz method
Equivalent SDOF approximation and effective modal mass
Finite element modal analysis preview
Convergence, trial function, and boundary-condition compatibility

topics.title: Random Vibration and Spectral Description
topics.description: Introduce stochastic excitation, power spectral density, RMS response, and vibration environments.

children.title: Random Process Basics
children.description: Students learn how to describe vibration when excitation is uncertain or broadband.

children.title: Random process, stationary process, ergodic assumption, mean, variance, and RMS
Autocorrelation, cross-correlation, probability density, and ensemble average
White noise, colored noise, narrowband process, and broadband process
Gaussian process and non-Gaussian vibration environments
Power Spectral Density
children.description: This subtopic gives the main frequency-domain tool for random vibration.

children.title: Power spectral density, one-sided PSD, two-sided PSD, and units
Mean square response as area under PSD
Frequency resolution, bandwidth, and windowing effect
Input PSD, output PSD, and transfer function magnitude squared
Engineering Random Vibration Applications
children.description: The goal is to interpret real vibration environments and design tests.

children.title: Road roughness, wind loading, seismic excitation, acoustic excitation, and launch vibration
RMS acceleration, crest factor, fatigue damage spectrum, and response spectrum preview
Random vibration test specification and shaker testing
Reliability, fatigue, and comfort metrics

topics.title: Vibration Measurement, Signal Processing, and Experimental Modal Testing
topics.description: Measure vibration with sensors, data acquisition, FFTs, and experimental modal analysis methods.

children.title: Sensors and Data Acquisition
children.description: Students learn how vibration data are actually measured.

children.title: Accelerometer, velocity sensor, displacement probe, strain gauge, and tachometer
Piezoelectric accelerometer, MEMS accelerometer, sensitivity, and calibration
Sampling rate, aliasing, anti-alias filter, and quantization
Mounting method, sensor mass loading, and cable effects
Signal Processing for Vibration
children.description: This subtopic turns raw time signals into interpretable vibration features.

children.title: Time waveform, FFT, spectrum, spectrogram, and order spectrum
Window function, leakage, averaging, and frequency resolution
Filtering, RMS, peak, peak-to-peak, and envelope detection
Coherence, cross spectrum, and transfer function estimate
Experimental Modal Testing
children.description: The point is to identify dynamic properties from measured input-output data.

children.title: Impact hammer, electrodynamic shaker, roving hammer, roving accelerometer, and reference sensor
FRF measurement, accelerance, mobility, receptance, and curve fitting
Natural frequency, damping ratio, mode shape, and modal assurance criterion
Test planning, boundary condition simulation, and validation

topics.title: Nonlinear Vibration, Stability, and Special Phenomena
topics.description: Survey nonlinear stiffness, damping, self-excitation, parametric excitation, and stability concepts.

children.title: Sources of Nonlinearity
children.description: Students learn why real systems may not obey linear superposition.

children.title: Geometric nonlinearity, material nonlinearity, contact nonlinearity, and clearance
Hardening spring, softening spring, cubic stiffness, and nonlinear damping
Backlash, friction, impact, and stop constraint
Amplitude-dependent frequency and response distortion
Nonlinear Response Phenomena
children.description: This subtopic names the behaviors students may see in real vibration data.

children.title: Jump phenomenon, hysteresis, subharmonic response, superharmonic response, and internal resonance
Limit cycle, self-excited vibration, and van der Pol oscillator
Parametric excitation, Mathieu equation, and instability tongue
Chaos, bifurcation, and strange attractor as advanced concepts
Stability and Approximate Nonlinear Methods
children.description: The goal is to give students entry points without turning the course into nonlinear dynamics only.

children.title: Equilibrium stability, perturbation, phase portrait, and basin of attraction
Linearization about equilibrium and local stability
Harmonic balance, describing function, and perturbation method preview
Practical screening for nonlinear effects in tests and simulations

topics.title: Engineering Applications, Vibration Control, and Design Project
topics.description: Apply vibration analysis to machines, vehicles, structures, rotating equipment, acoustics, and product design.

children.title: Application Domains
children.description: Students connect vibration theory to design and diagnosis contexts.

children.title: Rotating machinery, vehicle suspension, building vibration, aerospace structures, and precision equipment
Gear vibration, bearing fault, shaft misalignment, blade vibration, and panel vibration
Human exposure, comfort, noise, fatigue, and durability
Acoustics, structure-borne sound, and noise-control connection
Vibration Control Strategies
children.description: This subtopic compares ways to reduce vibration at the source, path, or receiver.

children.title: Resonance avoidance, stiffness tuning, mass tuning, damping addition, and isolation
Tuned mass damper, constrained-layer damping, dynamic absorber, and active control
Balancing, alignment, maintenance, and condition monitoring
Design trade-offs: weight, cost, temperature, durability, space, and performance
Design or Diagnosis Project
children.description: The final project asks students to synthesize modeling, measurement, and design judgement.

children.title: Problem statement, system model, assumptions, and parameters
Analytical prediction, simulation, measurement plan, and validation
Frequency response, modal result, isolation design, or fault diagnosis
Recommendation, uncertainty, limitations, and engineering communication
